comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Fresh reproduction on current origin/main (2026-08-10): two normal bug closes durably reached status=closed, then the post-close `metrics.blame._find_fixing_commit -> _resolves_to -> resolve_ticket_id` scan treated historical four-character commit subjects as ticket references. It emitted successive ambiguous-prefix errors for `b2bb`, `28f9`, `a9dd`, `dbb2`, and `3e8b` and kept scanning instead of terminating promptly. This is a sibling of the reported enrichment-drain symptom: the shared unsafe assumption is that an unqualified four-hex fragment is a resolvable ticket reference. The affected surface here is optional caused-by derivation after the close event, not enrichment queue reduction. The durable closes were unaffected; the local post-write process required interruption after status confirmation.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12: the leading '<id>:' commit-subject short form is NOT a supported citation form. Narrow enrichment-drain/blame ref resolution to [rebar:<id>] tokens and full canonical ids; leading-subject short-form tokens must no longer resolve as ticket references in prose/blame scanning. (Commit-convention subjects remain fine as commit style; they just are not citation evidence.)

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATOR DECISION REFINED 2026-08-12: 4-digit (single-quad) short IDs are DEPRECATED as a reference form — escalating collisions make them a pain point. Do NOT break existing 4-digit usage (compatibility resolution stays), but stop advertising them: docs and agent guidance should name the preferred forms — alias (preferred), 8-digit (two-quad) prefix, full canonical id, Jira/bridge ids. For THIS bug's fix: the enrichment-drain prose scanner must stop treating bare 4-hex fragments as ticket prefixes (the collision class measured here) — use the existing quiet-resolution seam; commit-subject and explicit-reference resolution keep today's behavior. Also sweep docs/agent guidance (AGENTS.md, docs/*) to stop advertising 4-digit references.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
TRIAGE EVIDENCE 2026-08-11 (pre-implementation, no code changed): the enrichment-drain attribution in this ticket is incorrect, and BOTH limbs are the same defect in src/rebar/metrics/blame.py.

1) The enrichment drain has NO prose scanner. Traced the full post-write subtree: _store/event_append.py:606 write_and_push -> _maybe_enrich_drain -> llm/enrich_drain.py:216 maybe_drain -> drain (:117) -> llm/enrich.py enrich -> llm/overlap/{queue,digest_sidecar}. Every ticket id in that subtree comes from os.listdir(tracker), i.e. an already-canonical directory name, which short-circuits on the fast path at _ids.py:239-241 and never reaches the >=4-char prefix branch (_ids.py:291-312) that prints 'Ambiguous prefix'. enrich.py:27-44 reads title/description/comments ONLY to assemble the LLM prompt; it never regex-scans that prose for ticket refs. Neither extract_ticket_refs nor a free-text resolve exists anywhere in llm/enrich.py, llm/enrich_drain.py, or llm/overlap/*. retrieve/judge/graph/wire are not on the drain path (they are reached from plan-review via wire.overlap_findings). Additionally, in the default async mode the drain child's stderr is redirected to .rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log (enrich_drain.py:193,209), so it could not have produced terminal noise even hypothetically.

2) The actual emitter is metrics/blame.py:55 (_resolves_to), reached only from _commands/transition_close.py:246-248 _apply_caused_by (gated on target_status=closed AND ticket_type=bug), which runs AFTER the close commits. Candidates come from verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs, whose second source is the leading '<token>:' of the commit subject (verify_commit.py:78-81); a bare 4-hex subject prefix passes _is_safe and falls through to the ambiguous-prefix print. Unlike close_precheck.py:119, blame passes neither quiet=True nor a resolution cache. This matches the second reproduction comment exactly (b2bb, 28f9, a9dd, dbb2, 3e8b during two bug closes).

3) The post-write HANG limb is now PROVEN, same file, same call: _find_fixing_commit (blame.py:60-72) runs 'git log --format=%H%x1f%B%x1e' over the ENTIRE branch history and calls _resolves_to per commit. _resolves_to recomputes resolve_ticket_id(bug_id, tracker) on EVERY commit, and any non-full/short/Jira id (an alias, or a bare 4-hex fragment) falls through to _scan_alias (_ids.py:170-217), which iterates every ticket directory and opens up to two JSON files per ticket. Nothing is memoized. Measured on this checkout: 3823 ticket directories, 2137 commits, 620 of which carry a bare '<4hex>:' subject; one unresolvable 4-hex candidate costs ~0.26s. The per-commit bug_id re-resolution alone is ~2137 x 0.26s ~= 9 minutes of pure alias scanning after the close has already committed, plus ~620 x 0.26s for the subject candidates. That is the 'lingering process', not a deadlock: an unbounded O(commits x tickets) scan in optional caused-by derivation.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE: the decided fix ('the enrichment-drain prose scanner must stop treating bare 4-hex fragments as prefixes; commit-subject resolution keeps today's behavior') has no implementable target -- the drain scanner does not exist, and the only defective path is precisely the commit-subject resolution that the decision excludes. Awaiting an operator call on which limb to change. The docs sweep (stop advertising 4-digit references in AGENTS.md and docs/*) is unaffected and remains valid as specified.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE 2026-08-11 — one plan premise was wrong; the guard is sound for a better reason, and is stricter than the plan authorized.

The plan justified restricting the short-circuit to 1-, 2-, and 4-quad hex forms by asserting those 'cannot collide with an alias' because wordlist aliases are adj-noun / adj-noun-noun. That premise is FALSE: 'dead' is in ticket-wordlist-v2.txt, and both 'dead' and 'deed' are in ticket-wordlist.txt, so 'dead-deed' is a generatable two-word alias that also has hex-quad shape. The plan-review E4 advisory flagged exactly this and was right.

The guard is sound anyway, via CONTROL FLOW in _ids.resolve_ticket_id rather than wordlist content:
- 4-quad matches _FULL_ID_RE and returns the exact-name lookup before the alias scan;
- 2-quad matches _SHORT_ID_RE, whose branch ends in an unconditional 'return None' before the alias scan, so even a real hex-shaped stored alias does not resolve by that name;
- 1-quad cannot be an alias at all (aliases are two or three words, or an 8-char no-dash fallback), and the implementation additionally never skips a ref equal to the target's own effective alias, covering a pathological stored alias;
- 3-quad forms DO reach the alias scan and are excluded from the short-circuit entirely.

The alias-collision test therefore asserts the real invariant instead of the plan's wording: it builds a tracker whose OTHER ticket has stored alias 'dead-deed' and asserts resolve_ticket_id('dead-deed', tracker) is None, i.e. skipping it changes no outcome. The implementation skips a strict subset of what the plan authorized, so no acceptance criterion is weakened.

Deliberately NOT done: the 'bound the history walk' idea (a git log --max-count cap). With the short-circuit the walk is O(commits) string comparisons and zero filesystem work, so a cap buys nothing measurable, and it WOULD change behavior — capping the log silently stops finding the fixing commit for older bugs, conflicting with the constraint that this change alter no resolution outcomes. The existing 300s _GIT_TIMEOUT watchdog still covers a wedged filesystem.

Verified RED before GREEN: against the pre-fix blame.py the new tests fail 10/15, including the two noise tests failing with the exact reported text 'Error: Ambiguous prefix ...'; the 5 behaviour-preservation tests pass against BOTH versions, which is the negative control proving resolution semantics are unchanged.

Follow-up worth its own ticket (NOT fixed here): _engine_support/lookups.py:47 GENERATES display ids as the 'shortest unambiguous dash-stripped prefix (min 4 chars)', so rebar still PRINTS the very 4-digit form these docs now deprecate. Changing that is a user-visible behavior change and was out of scope.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Closing a **bug** ticket sprays `Error: Ambiguous prefix '<4hex>' matches multiple tickets`
lines at the terminal and then leaves the CLI running for minutes after the close has already
committed durably. Reproduced twice (2026-08-08, 2026-08-10) with fragments `b2bb`, `28f9`,
`a9dd`, `dbb2`, `3e8b`, `03ef`, `94a3`, `c5b3`, `18ae`, `4527`; each time the operator had to
interrupt the process after confirming the status change had landed.

This ticket originally attributed the noise to the enrichment drain. That is **wrong**, and the
correction is recorded in a triage comment: the drain subtree
(`_store/event_append.py:606` -> `llm/enrich_drain.py:216` -> `drain` -> `llm/enrich.py`)
resolves only ticket ids that came from `os.listdir(tracker)`, i.e. already-canonical directory
names that short-circuit on the fast path at `_ids.py:239-241` and never reach the prefix
branch that prints. It has no prose scanner at all, and in async mode its stderr goes to
`.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log`.

## Approach

Both symptoms are ONE defect in `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, the optional `caused_by`
derivation invoked from `_commands/transition_close.py:246-248` **after** a bug close commits.
`_find_fixing_commit` walks the entire branch history and calls `_resolves_to` per commit;
`_resolves_to` re-resolves `bug_id` on **every** commit, and every candidate from
`verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (whose second source is the leading `<token>:` of the
commit subject) is resolved with no `quiet=`, no cache, and no shape filter. Any candidate that
is not a full/short/Jira id falls through to `_scan_alias`, which opens up to two JSON files
for each ticket directory.

Measured on this checkout: 3823 ticket directories, 2137 commits, 620 of them carrying a bare
`<4hex>:` subject (487 distinct), and ~0.26s per unresolvable candidate. The per-commit
`bug_id` re-resolution alone is ~2137 x 0.26s ~= 9 minutes of pure alias scanning. That is the
"hang": an unbounded O(commits x tickets) scan, not a deadlock.

Four changes, none of which alter WHICH id forms resolve:

1. Pass `quiet=True` at EVERY scanner call site in the module — `_resolves_to` (`blame.py:53`
   and `:55`), `_commit_ticket` (`:100`, the culprit commit's own subject), and the final
   self-comparison in `derive_caused_by` (`:135`) — using the seam `_ids.py:221-230` already
   documents for "scanners resolving candidates the user never supplied", the same treatment
   `_commands/close_precheck.py:119` already applies. Kills the terminal noise. All four are
   required: `_commit_ticket` is a SECOND scanner over commit-message candidates, so leaving it
   loud would keep a residual path that violates AC 1.
2. Hoist the `bug_id` resolution out of the per-commit loop (it is loop-invariant).
3. Memoize ref -> resolution for the duration of one derivation, as `close_precheck` does.
4. Short-circuit on a **necessary condition** before touching the store: a ref of hex-quad
   shape can only resolve to the target if the target's canonical id starts with it. This is
   provably semantics-preserving and is restricted to 1-, 2-, and 4-quad hex forms, which
   cannot collide with an alias (aliases are `adj-noun` or `adj-noun-noun` from the wordlist,
   or an 8-hex no-dash fallback) — 3-quad forms are deliberately excluded and still take the
   real resolver. Because that is a cross-module invariant owned by `_ids`/`_alias`, the guard
   carries a comment naming its source and a test asserts no generatable alias can take the
   hex-quad shape the short-circuit rejects, so the optimization cannot silently drift.

Separately, sweep the docs to stop advertising bare 4-digit (single-quad) references, per the
operator decision: name alias (preferred), 8-digit two-quad prefix, full canonical id, and
Jira/bridge ids as the reference forms. Compatibility resolution is unchanged and stays
documented as compatibility.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py` — the four changes above.
- `tests/unit/` — new regression tests.
- `src/rebar/_ids.py` — **module docstring only** (no code change): it is the one place that
  literally advertises "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as a supported form.
- `AGENTS.md` — the ticket-identifier authoring paragraph (:66-73). It does NOT advertise a
  bare 4-digit form today (it already discourages copying a short hex prefix and already frames
  short forms as compatibility), so this is an ADDITION: positively name the preferred forms,
  including the 8-digit two-quad prefix, which the file never mentions.

A repo-wide survey found the advertising surface is small: those two places. The ~420 bare
4-hex mentions elsewhere in `docs/` are incidental HISTORICAL citations of specific tickets
("epic 716f", "bug 84aa"), not guidance telling a reader to use that form, so they are out of
scope — rewriting them would be a large no-value diff. `docs/cli-reference.md:387`
(`rebar resolve <id_or_alias_or_prefix>`) is generated from `src/rebar/_cli/help/resolve.txt`
and says "prefix" generically, which correctly includes the PREFERRED 8-digit two-quad prefix,
so it is left alone.

Explicitly NOT changed: `_ids.py` resolution semantics, `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs`
(commit-subject candidates keep resolving exactly as today), the close gate, and the `Verified`
trailer check. No id form gains or loses the ability to resolve.

## Testing

- A commit message whose subject is a bare `<4hex>:` prefix that matches multiple tickets
  produces **no** `Ambiguous prefix` text on stderr during `derive_caused_by`.
- A bounded-work test: over a synthetic history of many commits carrying distinct 4-hex
  subjects, the number of underlying `resolve_ticket_id` calls stays small and constant rather
  than growing with the commit count (asserted by counting calls through a patched resolver).
- Behavior preservation: `derive_caused_by` still finds the fixing commit and the culprit
  ticket when the commit cites the bug by full canonical id, by 8-hex two-quad prefix, by
  alias, and by an unambiguous bare 4-hex prefix.
- A ref that is a hex-quad shape but NOT a prefix of the target still returns "no match", and a
  3-quad hex form still reaches the real resolver.
- A culprit commit whose OWN subject is an ambiguous bare 4-hex prefix also produces no
  `Ambiguous prefix` text (the `_commit_ticket` path).
- An alias-shape guard test: no alias generatable from the wordlist can take the 1-, 2-, or
  4-quad hex shape the short-circuit rejects.
- Docs: an assertion-style check that the swept files no longer present bare 4-digit ids as a
  recommended reference form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Closing a bug emits no `Ambiguous prefix` diagnostics for commit-subject candidates the
      user never supplied.
- [ ] `derive_caused_by` performs work bounded by the number of DISTINCT candidate refs rather
      than re-resolving per commit, proven by a call-count regression test.
- [ ] Every id form that resolves today still resolves: full canonical id, 8-hex two-quad
      prefix, alias, Jira key, and unambiguous bare 4-hex.
- [ ] The original post-close reproduction, replayed as a regression test over a synthetic
      multi-commit history, emits no `Ambiguous prefix` text and resolves each DISTINCT ref at
      most once (no per-commit re-resolution of the bug id).
- [ ] A regression test asserts that no alias generatable from the wordlist (`adj-noun`,
      `adj-noun-noun`, or the 8-hex no-dash fallback) can take the 1-, 2-, or 4-quad hex shape
      rejected by the short-circuit, so the optimization cannot silently drift.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_ids.py`'s module docstring no longer presents "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as
      a plain supported form, and `AGENTS.md`'s ticket-identifier paragraph positively names the
      preferred forms (alias / 8-digit two-quad prefix / full canonical id / Jira ids) while
      retaining its existing compatibility framing.

file_impact.reason: quiet scanner resolution, hoist loop-invariant target resolution, memoize refs, necessary-condition short-circuit
regression tests: no ambiguity stderr, bounded resolve-call count, all id forms still resolve
module docstring only: stop advertising >=4-char prefix as a supported reference form
name preferred ticket reference forms; mark bare 4-digit as compatibility-only
